name: 02-first-look-esp32
description: The device that just came back: every module, and what sits inside each one.

steps.title: Your device
steps.caption: Your device. Every module, top to bottom.
Control: a remote, a button or a fader, pointed at anything on this page.
Layouts: where your lights physically are.
Grid: width, height and depth. This one is sixty four by sixty four, which is four thousand and ninety six lights on a device that costs a few euros.
Effects: what they show, stacked in layers.
Layer: one effect and its modifiers, blended onto the ones below.
Drivers: how the finished frame reaches the lights.
An output driver is added per device rather than built in, so here is one: RMT, the peripheral that clocks a LED strip on this chip.
It drives the single light on the device itself, which is the cheapest way to see that a frame is really being rendered.
And a second one for the real strip. Each driver owns its own pin, so a device with several strips has several of these.
This is the one wired to the panel: a pin, a light count, and the preset that says which channel does what.
A driver does not have to drive a wire at all. This one sends the finished frame over the network instead.
ArtNet, E one point three one or DDP, to anything that listens: the same frame the strip gets, addressed to another device.
System: the device itself, its chip, its uptime, how fast it renders.
Tasks: what runs each frame, and what each costs in microseconds.
I2cScan: finds the chips on the I2C bus.
Pins: which pin every module has claimed, so two never fight over one.
File Manager: every file on the device, and one button that backs them all up.
Network: the WiFi it joined, and the other devices it can see.
Mqtt: a broker, for a home automation system.
Devices: every other MoonLight on the network, found on their own.
Services: the inputs.
Audio: this device has a microphone, so it is listening to the room.
Firmware: it finds the next release and installs it over the air.
MoonCloud: see what everyone else is running.
Stats: what this device shares, and the totals it gets back.
Talk: ask a question without leaving the page.
